svg.title: What USPS pages say about a Missing Mail search: check tracking first, file online starting 7 days after mailing, what to have ready, items USPS says it cannot search for, and what happens after you submit.
svg.text: USPS Missing Mail search
What the USPS pages say
First, check tracking
Both pages say to check USPS Tracking first.
The FAQ then lists waits for some services:
Priority Mail Express 7 or more days,
Domestic Registered Mail 14 or more,
Parcel Select 14 or more.
File online
Sign in or register at MissingMail.USPS.com.
Earliest: 7 days after mailing. Latest: 365
days after mailing. Drafts expire after 7
days. Customer Care cannot file it for you.
Have ready
Sender and recipient addresses, mailing date,
tracking numbers if you have them, container
type, size and color, a detailed description
of the contents, and photos if available.
USPS says it cannot search for
Hazardous material, live ammunition, opened
hair or beauty products, over-the-counter or
prescription drugs, perishables or food.
Handguns: returned only to a licensed dealer.
After you submit
Statuses: Accepted, Mailpiece Found, Expired,
Rejected, Canceled. A search runs until it
expires. USPS says a search does not
guarantee a successful outcome.
Sources: USPS FAQ (May 19, 2026) and USPS.com;
read Nov. 13, 2026
